- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, suggesting overshoot after spikes.
- Mean reversion is underappreciated — model fails to recognize that prices often revert to lower levels after recent spikes.
- Forecast bias is stronger in the first 5–10 days, with error decreasing as forecast horizon extends.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — it takes too long to adjust downward.
- Overshooting is more common after high historical peaks; model fails to cap forecasts near recent highs.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day horizon, suggesting horizon-specific decay or misalignment with true trend.
